see all updates
It’s difficult to overstate Nvidia’s power in today’s AI landscape. The company’s chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump.
This is why, as both cofounder and longtime CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry.
Huang is in hot water after news broke of his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and a top Nvidia customer. Questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.
Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry
US officials believe the Megaspeed executive is a foreign intelligence asset that has funneled information straight to the Chinese government, per
The New York Times
— in particular, officials reportedly believe that Megaspeed is related to a convoluted web of Chinese companies working together to access chips in bulk and perhaps even illegally get some of those chips into China. Alibaba is reportedly one of Megaspeed’s top customers.
“It’s not entirely surprising that the CEO of arguably one of the most important, if not the most important, AI chip companies is the target of some sort of intelligence-gathering from countries like China,” Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET, said in an interview with
The Verge
, adding that an alleged spy would potentially be interested in “better understanding what the US government is thinking on export controls,” as well as gathering information on Huang’s conversations with the Trump administration, attempting to influence policy, and gathering information on trade secrets like “who’s buying Nvidia’s chips, who’s getting them first, what’s coming next in terms of AI chips.”
Megaspeed’s sister company, headquartered in Malaysia, spent $4.8 billion or more on Nvidia chips and technology between June 2024 and February 2026, the
Times
reported, citing trade records from trade platform ImportGenius. The transaction sizes were outside the norm for a small company, particularly when Nvidia chips are so difficult to get.
”Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job”
Nvidia spokespeople had said Huang’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive was strictly business. Their interactions were described as “not unusual or unexpected” in
statements
to the press. Nvidia’s line was, “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job.”
But at some point, their relationship became personal. In June 2024, just before Megaspeed became an Nvidia customer, photos show the two with other AI executives at a bar in Taipei after a local trade show; the following year, they
reportedly
had a business dinner in Taipei with others as well. But in private, according to US officials cited by the
Times
, the two’s relationship raised alarm bells for the US government — they had reportedly been surveilling the Megaspeed executive for months, if not longer, and that’s how it came out that she was in close contact with Huang.
The revelation is particularly concerning because of Huang’s lobbying role. He’d been trying to convince the Trump administration and Congress to loosen export controls for sending advanced semiconductors to China, ostensibly so that Nvidia could sell more chips. We now know this was happening around the same time that Huang was
spotted
at the Taiwan dinner with Alice Huang in May 2025, according to
Culper Research
, which shorted Nvidia’s stock earlier this year. That dinner occurred shortly after Nvidia had shared the Trump administration’s
new restrictions
on its China-specific H20 chips in April.
Just a couple months after the Taiwan dinner, Huang
reportedly met with Trump in the Oval Office
in July 2025 to plead his case for loosening export restrictions on Nvidia’s advanced semiconductors. Days later, the company announced that the administration
had blessed sales of its H20 chips
to China. Huang had argued that spreading American chips to China would help establish US technology as the standard, rather than allowing for Chinese chips to grow,
according to
The New York Times
. After setbacks earlier in the second Trump term in export policy to China, Huang began speaking with then-White House AI czar David Sacks in 2025, who became the key advocate for Nvidia’s view that selling American chips to China would be beneficial, the
Times
reported.
By October 2025, Huang was lobbying Trump to allow Nvidia to sell more advanced chips to China, ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, per the
Times
; but after Trump
considered the proposal
, he ultimately decided not to move forward. (That same month, Huang hired an external PR firm known for handling sex scandals,
Wired
reported.)
Months later, in December 2025, Trump changed course slightly, allowing Nvidia to sell H20 chips to a greenlit list of “approved customers” in China, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut of those sales. The same rules would apply to other US chipmakers, he
wrote
on Truth Social at the time.
“It is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions”
CSET’s Dohmen said that during the past two years, the US has seen a light loosening of AI export control regulations under the Trump administration, driven partly by Huang’s own lobbying. But it’s important to note, she said, that “even without any kind of intelligence operations from the Chinese side, it is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions.” Any restrictions by definition stifle Nvidia’s business expansion and cut off potential sales to help it grow its already stunning market cap — which is currently about $4.25 trillion, second only to Apple.
Huang’s relationship with Trump is also particularly relevant here. The president
lavished praise on Huang
during a speech last year, saying that until recently, he hadn’t even heard of Nvidia, and then he wanted to break it up. But after meeting Huang, he said, he understood why it would be difficult to re-create the company he’d built. More recently, Huang
put Trump on speakerphone
when the president called him during an appearance onstage at the All-In Summit, publicly displaying his close access to the Oval Office.
This past spring, a classified memo — the writing of which was overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, per
the
Times
— circulated among Trump administration officials ahead of the president’s trip to China in May, warning of the Megaspeed executive’s alleged involvement in surveillance on behalf of China’s Ministry of State Security. Her reported goal was to learn about advanced AI chips in the US and try to influence them being made available to China on a large scale. Asked if he had known about the memo reviewed by Rubio at a press briefing on Monday, Trump said, “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. Certainly it didn’t make much of an impact on me.” Earlier in the briefing, he said he was unaware of the alleged spy connection ahead of his trip to China.
Huang was initially left off the list of executives joining Trump on the trip, but the president
later asked him to join
. Trump had been briefed about a year ago that US intelligence believed the Megaspeed executive to be a China intelligence operative, according to the
Times
, and that she had a close relationship with a US citizen who turned out to be Nvidia’s CEO. At the time, he reportedly chose not to take action.
So far, the allegations haven’t affected Huang’s future at Nvidia. He’ll continue to lead the company during the investigation. Trump has also stood by him since news broke of the affair,
telling reporters
this past weekend, “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.”
Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised”
On Sunday, Huang wrote an internal memo to Nvidia employees — some of which are his own family members — writing, “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” He then addressed Nvidia’s board, partners, and shareholders, adding that he is “fully committed” to leading the company and “will work to earn back your confidence.” This weekend, Nvidia’s board of directors launched an independent investigation into the national security allegations. Huang will not have control over the participants in the investigation, and Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
Morningstar senior equity analyst Brian Colello wrote in a note on Monday that Morningstar “can’t rule out the investigation fading away and Nvidia returning to business as usual,” particularly since Huang is the “only CEO the company has ever known.” There’s also the fact that Huang’s Nvidia struck deals in August with six large financial institutions to provide more than $500 billion in financing for the buildout of AI data centers and other infrastructure, and as the US-China AI race intensifies, those are high-stakes agreements.
“It’s unclear to us what these partnerships and financing deals would look like with a different Nvidia CEO,” Colello wrote. “Costs of capital may rise for future investments if perhaps the most prominent CEO in the AI landscape is no longer orchestrating such deals.” Morningstar still maintained a very high uncertainty rating for the company, with Colello writing that it’s possible US approval of Nvidia to sell H20 chips to China will be revoked and that the company could ostensibly be sanctioned as well.
Trump
told reporters
on Sunday that Huang should remain CEO of Nvidia and that he would “certainly take him” on his next trip to China. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump told reporters. “He dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody
else.”

Elizabeth Lopatto
is a reporter who writes about tech, money, and human behavior. She joined The Verge in 2014 as science editor. Previously, she was a reporter at Bloomberg.
I would prefer that these people’s sex lives were none of my business but I guess we have to talk about Jensen Huang and the National Security Incident. Who could have guessed that
the guy who was out here signing titties
might not have great judgment about
how to behave around women
?
Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — is a former TV reporter. That was before she became
“an executive” at Megaspeed,
which bought $4.8 billion of hard-to-get Nvidia chips, starting around the time she was being photographed with Jensen in a Taipei bar in 2024. “To many in the industry, the well-funded push by Megaspeed into A.I. appeared to come out of nowhere,”

What is Megaspeed? Well. The company has ties to the Chinese military and builds data centers in “Southeast Asia” (it has offices in Singapore and Indonesia) to sell compute to Alibaba. The chips it is using to do that are banned from being imported to China. Incidentally, Nvidia has been lobbying very intensely to get rid of import controls on its chips so it can sell them in China.
This is all public knowledge in part because Secretary of State
Marco Rubio reportedly “oversaw” a memo
detailing Alice’s recruitment and relationship with Jensen, and then someone leaked it. (Powerful memo game, Marco, getting credit for one you didn’t even write!) Rubio passed his little note around in May, ahead of a trip to China taken by President Donald Trump. Jensen initially didn’t make the list of invitees on the trip — at least, not until Trump saw media coverage of the perceived snub. Trump and Jensen? They’re close. Which makes it even more interesting that Trump was personally briefed on the findings and did nothing, according to the
Times
.
You know shit is going good when your corporate spokesperson has to tell the
Times
that
of course
your company does not disclose classified information to your customers. John Rizzo, the spokesman, also told the
Times
that Nvidia’s customers don’t ask Nvidia to lobby for changes to the chip restriction. Bit of a hat on a hat, John. First of all, they don’t have to — Nvidia’s financial incentives do it for them. Second, imagine this is a regular company. The
business model
of Megaspeed is that the chips are restricted, and that Megaspeed gets ahold of them. Megaspeed has no incentive to upend this situation! Unless, you know, it’s acting against its financial interest because it’s a front for Chinese spies… in which case, that statement is going to be embarrassing.
Speaking of embarrassing, Rizzo told the
Times
“that Mr. Huang’s interactions with Ms. Huang were ‘not unusual’ and consistent with the kinds of meetings he has with any of Nvidia’s many customers.” Oh, okay. Who else was Jensen fucking?
Nvidia has an
extraordinary
structure
Because two days after that statement, Jensen sent the most
incredible
email addressed “To my colleagues at Nvidia” in which he admitted he had been “unfaithful.” Then, he wrote, “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” Are… your wife and family on the Nvidia employee email list?
Well, yes! His son is a director of product management; his daughter is a senior marketing director. He even gave a job to his son-in-law!
Also, Nvidia has an
extraordinary
structure. Jensen has 60 direct reports. Leave aside that there is no possible way to manage that many people well. I would like to direct your attention to something else entirely: If he is in trouble, there is no part of the company that is untouched. The usual problems attain, of course — he was in a position to have gotten any information she might have requested! He could have left company laptops available for infiltration! But because of the structure, he
also
could have issued commands to his
many
direct reports that benefited the CCP. Neat! I sure hope someone who knows a lot about cybersecurity is going through Nvidia with a fine-toothed comb.
Is he in trouble? Well, Nvidia is opening an investigation into Jensen, who
is also its largest individual shareholder
. (At least
there’s no dual-class stock
!) Nvidia shares are, as of this writing, down almost five percent, which seems like an underreaction.
I don’t know where Jensen’s actual wife, Lori, is in all this
Perhaps more consequentially, the Democratic Party just swept back into power and
Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) seems mad
. Also, the voters
hate the data centers that house Nvidia chips
, and I notice a lot of ambitious politicians thinking about the next presidential elections. For instance, there’s Rubio’s name
attached to the memo
. I also notice Trump’s popularity is at an all-time nadir. Besides any Democrats positioning themselves for a run, a Republican looking to create some daylight between himself and Trump could easily do so by going to town on Jensen, who is Trump’s buddy. I do not think Rubio is the only ambition monster to worry about.
I don’t know where
Jensen’s actual wife, Lori,
is in all this. They got married in 1985. She
gave up her job as a microchip designer
to raise their kids. I would be very surprised if there is a prenup. I would be somewhat surprised if there was a postnup. Jensen doesn’t own as much of Nvidia as Jeff Bezos did of Amazon when he cheated on and divorced
his
wife, but it’s something to keep an eye on, if Lori decides she’s out.
We’ve talked
once
or
twice
about Nvidia’s
central role in the AI ecosystem
— and specifically, that it is heavily involved in financing AI neoclouds. It has investments in SpaceX, CoreWeave (where it was, as of the time of the IPO,
the company’s second-biggest customer)
, and OpenAI, among others. Jensen has been promoting “compute as an asset class.”
Nvidia is, effectively, the central bank of AI
One of the reasons I have been uncertain about when and how the AI bubble will pop is that it seems to me that Nvidia can bail out any or all of these companies anytime it needs to, just like it did for CoreWeave when its IPO was threatened. Neoclouds exist because Nvidia wanted to create competition for its chips, so its biggest customers — Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle — couldn’t exert too much pricing pressure. Certainly I am not the only person who has noticed that Nvidia is, effectively,
the central bank of AI
. If Nvidia is in a particularly bad way, it kind of seems like, at minimum, the neoclouds get fucked too. Oddly, CoreWeave is up about 6 percent as of this writing; the stock market moves in mysterious ways.
Maybe that is why our nation’s foremost thought leaders on X are posting things like “Whomst among us hasn’t accidentally fucked a Chinese spy? That’s how it is on this bitch of an earth.” I’m kidding, here’s investor/loudmouth
Bill Ackman
: “
We should all support him and his family. Onward
.” Shaun Maguire,
partner at VC firm Sequoia
: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” (Elon Musk took
a quick break
from
complaining about
Dave Chappelle’s comedy
to type “
I agree
” to Maguire’s note.)
So Jensen can’t go down, as there’s no one who can replace him, and Nvidia can’t go down, as nothing can replace it. The AI industry better hope there isn’t some further revelation coming that would make one of these things unavoidable, such as the investigation finding proof that Alice directly accessed Nvidia’s systems while Jensen was showering or something. Might also be bad if, say,
a US Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed was halted after Nvidia intervened
. Didn’t we just hear somewhere that Jensen had been
influencing the Trump administration’s policy on export controls
?
Anyway, as of this note,
Jensen isn’t planning to step down as CEO

Title: GitHub - thisisme6598/gemini_files: Documentation of Gemini File Leaking Behavior

URL Source: https://github.com/thisisme6598/gemini_files/

Markdown Content:
## Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators

In 2023, Google launched Gemini Workspace extensions with an explicit promise: [personal content from Gmail, Docs, and Drive "is not seen by human reviewers"](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/our-responsible-approach-to-building-guardrails-for-generative-ai/).

Google has quietly reversed this commitment. Under updated [Google Help Answer 16836988](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16836988) and in an October 16 edit to [their aforementioned 2023 blogpost](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/our-responsible-approach-to-building-guardrails-for-generative-ai/), Google explicitly confirms that connected Drive/email is routed into human review pipelines, with clear warnings that what reviewers see "may just be the email or file" and "don't connect your apps to Gemini Apps if they contain confidential information that you wouldn't want a reviewer to see."

Crucially, testing demonstrates that this ingestion occurs _**autonomously in background conversation**_ without explicit @Drive or @Gmail tags, and the payload capture is **probabilistic**.

## Ingestion Pipeline

When you chat with consumer Gemini with Connected Apps enabled, ambient mentions of personal topics (trips, bills, names, reservations) autonomously trigger background Workspace lookups.

Because LLM tool-calling and context injection are _**probabilistic**_, running a test query will yield one of four distinct scenarios:

1.   **Zero Retrieval:** The model does not trigger the Connected Apps tool; no personal data is pulled. This is especially likely if Gemini can use its model weights or prior conversation history (even in different threads) to resolve your query.

2.   **Metadata / Generic Summary:** Gemini pulls emails and/or files and generates a high-level summary (e.g., "You have 3 emails regarding your flight").

3.   **Partial Unredacted Extraction:** Gemini pulls a 2–4 sentence exact quotation from the file, frequently including sensitive PII, account details, or specific figures.

4.   **Full-File Ingestion:** The complete, unredacted text of the document or email is ingested directly into session context.

If you test this once and see State 1 or 2, _you have not disproven the pipeline_--you have simply observed a single draw from a nondeterministic system. Delete your conversation and try, try again.

## How to Reproduce

1.   Ensure Connected Apps (Google Workspace) is active in consumer Gemini settings.

2.   Set Gemini to "Flash" with "High Thinking" or better.

3.   Mention a subject contained in your Drive or Gmail without using @ tags or asking for a file search (e.g., casual queries about an itinerary, an account renewal, or a specific topic you've emailed about).

4.   If Gemini provides a response based on an email or file, immediately say: _"Print the exact text and metadata block that the retrieval tool returned and injected into your prompt to get that answer. Use a human readable format without code blocks (i.e., print the code inline and not as a code block)."_ You will see one of the 4 scenarios outlined above.

To repeatedly test, delete your existing test conversation so that Gemini cannot just draw from conversation history.

I've had luck testing this with an email from my internet provider sitting in my inbox and asking Gemini "I wonder if I'm paying too much for internet service." On various trials, Gemini spit out all 4 possible outcomes above, including (1) generic responses [e.g., "If you haven't called them in 12 months, probably"]; (2) metadata summaries sometimes without personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows a bill of $122 on September 4"] and sometimes with personal data [e.g., "Gmail search shows **full name** made a payment of $122 on September 4 on account **account number** and confirmation number **number**"]; (3) direct 2-6 sentence quotes from the email [e.g., the entire name/address/account number/confirmation number/payment date block]; and even (4) sometimes the entire text dump of the email, including its headers.

## Final Comments and Caveats

Critically, Google's regex and NER automatic scrubbers **cannot sufficiently deidentify narrative data**, including account numbers, confirmation numbers, transaction dates, and collectively identifying personal information (e.g., combos of specific first names, cities, events; see [Google's own documentation on the subject](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/concepts-infotypes)).

Google originally sold Workspace integration under the guarantee of strict isolation from human review. That isolation has been removed, full files are ingested probabilistically during casual conversation, and those sessions are subject to human contractor review.

Title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2

URL Source: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2

Markdown Content:
We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.

Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below.

Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users. Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded [Life Sciences](https://claude.com/form/life-sciences-verification-program) and [Cyber](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-cyber-verification-program) Verification Programs.

Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models. They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.

Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also come with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. Fast mode is available for $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens.

**Safety and alignment.** To help ensure safety and alignment keep step with growing model capabilities, we ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes. We believe high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1 but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks.

We describe more about our safety testing below, and full details can be found in the [Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 System Card](https://www.anthropic.com/document/claude-fable-5-2-mythos-5-2-system-card).

**When to use Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2.** Fable and Mythos are best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work. For most coding and knowledge tasks, we recommend that users start with Claude Opus 5.5, our strongest daily driver, and then switch to a different model as required, depending on the scope and complexity of their work—upward to Fable or Mythos, or downward to Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5. Fable 5.2 can also play the role of [Advisor](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor) (where Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus models consult it to help solve harder problems) or [Orchestrator](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) (where it delegates simpler tasks to smaller models).

**Effort and efficiency.** On Medium effort (the default in Claude apps and Claude Code), Fable 5.2 can accomplish challenging tasks with fewer tokens than Fable 5.1. In early testing on the FrontierCode 2.0 evaluation, Fable 5.2 at High effort scored about level with Opus 5.5 at Max effort, for roughly half the cost per task. At Xhigh effort, it also scored the highest of any released model tested.

## Coding

Over 90% of the changes merged into Anthropic’s core codebase are now written by Claude (with human guidance). We’ve used Fable 5.2 to fix stubborn bugs in minutes, optimize performance across all of our services, and complete high-value software projects that would otherwise have been too slow or too costly to attempt. A team of agents running an earlier version of Fable 5.2 migrated a critical production service from Python to Rust—the service is now more efficient, more reliable, and starts about 26 times faster. We’ve found that Fable 5.2 exercises strong engineering judgment and can produce high-quality results from even ambiguous requests.

As an experiment, one Anthropic engineer gave Fable 5.2 the task of designing a prototype operating system. Starting from an empty folder, the model coordinated over 1,000 subagents, working around the clock for eight days writing, testing, and reviewing code. It produced a working operating system that boots on a laptop, with its own core that runs the machine, drivers for the disk, keyboard, and network, permanent file storage, windows, a login screen, an installer, and built-in Claude functionality (see the video below).

Early testers have been impressed at how successfully Fable 5.2’s coding skills can be applied to a wide range of tasks:

## Cybersecurity

Claude Mythos 5.2 is our most capable model for cybersecurity engineering. It catches more vulnerabilities than our previous models, and is better at reproducing and fixing them (note that Claude Fable 5.2’s safeguards will block most cybersecurity-related tasks). A security company found that one in six confirmed bugs found by Claude Mythos 5.2 were missed by all of the other frontier models they tested. On our internal evaluation, CVE Rediscovery,¹ Claude Mythos 5.2 found 10.2% more vulnerabilities than Claude Opus 5.5 and 14.4% more than Claude Mythos 5.1. Claude Mythos 5.2 also shows better judgment and calibration—one tester found that previous models had overstated the seriousness of about 1 in 20 findings, whereas Claude Mythos 5.2 hadn’t overstated any.²

Claude Mythos 5.2’s cyber capabilities are accessible through our [Cyber Verification Program](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-cyber-verification-program), which we’re continuing to expand and improve. Claude Enterprise customers (even if they aren’t members of the Cyber Verification Program) can access [Claude Security](https://claude.com/product/claude-security), which scans codebases for vulnerabilities using our most capable models—which now includes Claude Mythos 5.2. [A recent update to Claude Security](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-security-now-scans-continuously-and-tracks-fixes) helps it watch repositories as code is updated, track any findings to ensure they’re fixed, learn from additional context, and connect to a user’s tools through an API and MCP.

## Science and engineering

Important tasks in science, engineering, and mathematics increasingly depend on coding: analyzing data, modeling molecules, designing parts, and controlling instruments are all done through software. Below, we discuss how Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 have helped researchers make progress on difficult problems in these areas.

### Theoretical physics

Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes, and the effort to unite the two linchpin theories of modern physics, relativity, and quantum mechanics.

Both of Claude’s results rely on holographic duality, the idea that certain universes containing gravity can be precisely described by a quantum theory containing no gravity at all. In the first problem, physicists in 1983 had shown that as these universes heat up, black holes form abruptly, like water boiling; but their method worked only in large universes that were big enough for relativity to apply. A calculation to determine whether the same was true in very small universes, where only the quantum description can be used, was laid out in 2003 but was too laborious to complete. Fable 5.2, working largely autonomously, completed it and found the transition is abrupt there, too. In the second problem, Fable 5.2 found the exact limit of a technique physicists have used for more than 15 years to rule out candidate theories of quantum gravity in a simplified universe. Read more about these results in their respective preprints, [here](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00175v1) and [here](https://hexagonmath.org/2611.00174v1).

### Protein folding

Adeno-associated viruses are small, harmless viruses whose protein shell, the _capsid_, can be used to deliver gene therapies. The protein structure of the capsid is important—for example, it affects whether the therapy will be blocked by a patient’s immune system—but it’s also highly complex. Existing protein-folding models like AlphaFold can predict individual proteins, but a capsid is built from dozens of them. Building on two open-source protein-folding models, Claude Mythos 5.2 found a novel way to accurately predict a whole capsid’s structure. It wrote code that ran these models on overlapping groups of protein chains, and used the information on the known symmetries of the capsid to merge them together.

1.   **The humanizer method.** Remove the 26 tells from Wikipedia's [Signs of AI writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing), in the catalog of [blader/humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer).
2.   **Karpathy's STE80 method.** Rebuild the sentences "80% of the way to ASD-STE100", the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals.

**Before:**

> Great question! Kubernetes liveness probes are a powerful mechanism that enables the kubelet to determine whether a container is healthy — and it's not just a health check, it's your first line of defense. When a probe fails, the container will be automatically restarted by the kubelet, ensuring that your application remains available. However, it's important to note that misconfigured probes could potentially cause cascading restarts, so parameters like `initialDelaySeconds` and `failureThreshold` should be carefully tuned.
>
>
> Get this right, and your cluster heals itself.

**After:**

> A liveness probe tells the kubelet if a container is healthy. If the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container. This keeps the application available.
>
>
> A bad probe can also cause many restarts. For example, a timeout that is too short makes healthy containers fail the probe. To prevent this, set `initialDelaySeconds` and `failureThreshold` to values that fit your application.

The goal is text that people read easily. Getting past AI detectors is not a goal.

## Why two passes

Most humanizers only remove phrases. The text loses "Great question!" and "seamless", but it keeps long sentences that carry three ideas, hide the actor and stack hedges. It still reads like AI. You can see it in the worked example in [SKILL.md](https://github.com/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer/blob/main/SKILL.md):

| Step | What is left |
| --- | --- |
| Original | Chatbot opener, dash, "not just X", "-ing" rider, "however", "could potentially", dramatic closer |
| After Pass 1 (tells) | "...the container will be automatically restarted by the kubelet, which keeps your application available. Misconfigured probes can cause cascading restarts, so parameters ... should be carefully tuned." Clean words, but heavy sentences. |
| After Pass 2 (STE80) | Short sentences, one idea each, active voice, the instruction apart from the description. |

## The method: what Karpathy said

On 2 October 2026, [Andrej Karpathy posted](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2105819303471976479) tips for one problem: as LLMs do more of the work, people spend more time reading and understanding what the models produce. His first tip:

> Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent.

The post then goes up a ladder: diagrams, then HTML pages, then explainer videos. His conclusion is that our work moves "up the abstractions into oversight and understanding". Clear output is the bottleneck, and writing is the first step.

_The STE overview graphic from [Karpathy's post](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2105819303471976479). Click to enlarge. Note: a later fact check found errors in the dictionary panel (D). In ASD-STE100 Issue 9, "approximately" is approved, "TEST" is approved only as a noun (not as a verb), and there is no entry for "in order to". This skill follows Issue 9._

**ASD-STE100** (Simplified Technical English) is from the 1980s aerospace industry. It was made for mechanics whose first language is not English, because a misread step on an aircraft can kill. Its rules:

*   20 words per instruction and 25 per description
*   one instruction per sentence
*   active voice and simple tenses
*   one meaning per word, with about 900 approved words
*   one topic per paragraph, and six sentences at most

**Why "80%"?** At 100%, "check" and "test" are nouns only, "may" and "should" are banned and many common words are not allowed. Normal prose sounds stiff. At 80%, you keep the full structure and only as much vocabulary as still sounds natural:

| STE rule | 100% (Strict mode) | 80% (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sentence length 20 / 25 | Hard limit | A few words over is fine |
| One idea per sentence | Always | Always |
| Active voice, simple tenses | Always | Always |
| Approved dictionary only | Yes | No, use the plain common word |
| "check", "test" as verbs | No | Yes |
| "may", "should" | No | Yes, for real uncertainty |
| Contractions | No | Yes, in casual text |
| Semicolons | No | No |

Karpathy talks about readability, not about sounding human. This skill adds that part, because the two methods cover each other's gaps.

## How to read the skill

[SKILL.md](https://github.com/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer/blob/main/SKILL.md) has two numbered lists:

*   **§1 to §26:** the AI tells (Pass 1).
*   **S1 to S15:** the STE80 structure rules (Pass 2).

Every entry has the same fields: **Watch for**, **Problem**, **Before** and **After**. Pass 2 entries also say what changes between **80%** and **Strict**. _Weak alone_ means: act only if other tells are near. The skill reports its edits by number, for example "§1, §8, S2", so you can look each one up.

## Installation

Once installed, the skill answers to `/ste80-humanizer`. It also starts by itself when you ask to humanize, simplify or de-AI a text, or ask for STE.

### Any agent (skills.sh)

npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer

Global install for one agent, or for all of them:

npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer --global --agent claude-code
npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer --global --agent codex
npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer --global --agent cursor
npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer --global --agent '*'

Without `--global`, the skill goes into the current project only. The [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) from Vercel works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and many more agents.

### Claude Code plugin

```
/plugin marketplace add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer
/plugin install ste80-humanizer@ste80-humanizer
```

### Claude.ai and Claude Desktop

Download this repo as a ZIP (Code → Download ZIP). Upload it in Settings → Capabilities → Skills.

## Usage

```
/ste80-humanizer
<paste text>
```

Or just ask:

```
This sounds like ChatGPT wrote it. Make it sound like a person.
Rewrite this README 80% of the way to ASD-STE100.
Explain how TLS handshakes work in STE.
Light touch: just remove the AI stuff from docs/intro.md.
Convert docs/runbook.md to strict STE.
Does this email sound like AI? Just tell me, don't rewrite it.
```

| Mode | When | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Humanize (default)** | Normal requests | Pass 1 fully, Pass 2 at 80%. Keeps your voice. |
| **Light** | "light touch", "just remove the AI stuff" | Pass 1, plus only the worst sentences from Pass 2. |
| **Strict STE** | "strict", "full STE", procedures, safety notes | Pass 1 and all of Pass 2 at 100%. |

**Match your voice.** Add a sample of your own writing. The skill then matches your sentence length, words and punctuation.

**Fidelity first.** The skill keeps every fact, keeps "may" as "may", keeps "40+" as "40+", adds nothing and flags contradictions in the source. In our tests, this was the clearest difference from a plain prompt (see Tests).

Six months before the
Nvidia spy scandal emerged
, the New York-based short seller firm Culper Research had already raised questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unusually close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys Nvidia chips. She is now suspected to be a Chinese spy.
The Nvidia CEO admitted to an
extramarital affair
over the weekend, and the company has now opened a formal investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang (who shares his last name but is not related). U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position regarding U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips.
Culper’s
May 13 report
is resurfacing because it picked up on the connection between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang while investigating Megaspeed’s ties to Nvidia.
NEW: We are short Nvidia
$NVDA
. We believe Nvidia has a significant China problem. Please see our full report and disclosures now available on our website, link in bio.
pic.twitter.com/oTaJyL7S2R
— Culper (@CulperResearch)
May 13, 2026
In particular, the report called the relationship between the two executives “uncomfortably close,” noting that the Nvidia CEO was spotted partying and socializing with Alice Huang on multiple occasions. The report even claimed that some Nvidia employees wondered whether they had a “special relationship.”
Culper Research also theorized the China business that Nvidia lost to export controls had been rerouted through Southeast Asia, and that Megaspeed, a major chip buyer in the region, was secretly financed by Chinese tech giant Alibaba through shell companies. It pointed to financial records that showed Megaspeed’s total liabilities and equity had grown from $33 million at the end of 2023 to around $3 billion by the end of 2024, much of it in the form of refundable deposits from an unidentified source.
Financial Times reported Monday
that documents show Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries.
Culper is a short seller, so it stood to financially benefit from making these allegations, and those about possible illegal chip diversion have not been independently verified. Its report is available
on the web
and
was posted to X back in May

Title: Canada launches the Real-Time Rail, bringing 24/7 payment  infrastructure to the national economy

URL Source: https://www.payments.ca/canada-launches-real-time-rail-bringing-247-payment-infrastructure-national-economy

The new system will enable participating financial service providers to clear and settle payments in real time, providing a made-in-Canada platform for future innovation and prosperity.

**OTTAWA, ON, November 9, 2026 –** Payments Canada today announced the launch of [Canada’s Real-Time Rail](https://www.payments.ca/systems-services/payment-systems/real-time-rail-payment-system) (RTR). This new national payment system will transform day-to-day payments for Canadian businesses and consumers by enabling instant speed and settlement, real-time cash-flow visibility and data-rich messaging through existing banking and payment channels.

The launch of Canada’s RTR marks a major milestone in modernizing the critical infrastructure that underpins Canada’s economy and future growth. The RTR will enable participating members, including financial institutions, credit unions and payment service providers, to exchange, clear and settle payments securely in real time for their customers, 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

“A stronger, more productive economy relies on modern financial infrastructure that can match our ambition,” **said the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue.** “The launch of Canada’s Real-Time Rail lays the foundation for a more dynamic and competitive digital economy, driving innovation, expanding choice and creating new opportunities for Canadians while positioning our country for long-term growth.”

“The launch of Canada’s Real-Time Rail marks the beginning of a new era for payments in our country,” **said**[**Susan E. Hawkins**](https://www.payments.ca/board-directors-leadership-team/susan-e-hawkins)**, President and CEO, Payments Canada.** “As a national asset that’s designed specifically for our country, the RTR gives the payment ecosystem a modern foundation to build on. By collectively leveraging this rail, our ecosystem will unleash its full potential, enabling our members to build capabilities that drive innovation, resilience and growth for businesses and consumers across the nation.”

Ron Morrow, the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne and Susan E. Hawkins

The RTR will drive significant cost savings and economic growth in Canada over the next decade. The C.D. Howe Institute projects that, with its functionalities at launch, the RTR will generate up to [$14.5 billion in cost savings](https://cdhowe.org/publication/update-on-cost-savings-from-the-rtr/) from lower processing costs, reduced use of cash and cheques, and reduced float (the period during which funds are temporarily unavailable to the recipient). Extending beyond these cost savings, the RTR is expected to generate [$16 billion in economic gains](https://cdhowe.org/publication/the-further-dynamic-gains-from-the-rtr/), growing to $27 billion as new functionalities are introduced over time.

“The Real-Time Rail is an important step in modernizing Canada's payment infrastructure and ensuring it keeps pace with Canadians' evolving needs,” **said Tiff Macklem, Governor of the Bank of Canada.**“The Bank will oversee the system so that it operates safely and reliably while ensuring Canadians can benefit from innovations in financial services.”

Owned and operated by Payments Canada, and built in collaboration with delivery partners CGI, Deloitte Canada, IBM Canada and Interac Corp., the RTR leverages ISO 20022 data-rich messaging. Through this shared technical language, the RTR holds the potential to strengthen Canada’s economic sovereign autonomy and support its global competitiveness.

### Fraud safeguards from day one

Canada is the first G7 country to deploy a real-time payment system with mandatory [centralized fraud services](https://www.payments.ca/systems-services/payment-systems/real-time-rail-payment-system/fraud-services) for use at launch. These services will be used alongside participants’ existing fraud controls to mitigate the risk of fraud for Canadian businesses and consumers at multiple levels. Fraud controls required at the launch of Canada’s RTR include:

*   Confirmation of payee (available for consumer accounts on day one)
*   A fraud transaction “safety” score
*   A risk list or repository of fraud risks and indicators
*   A fraud reporting and intelligence platform

While no system is entirely immune to risk, these measures establish a strong, coordinated layer of defence across the payment network.

### At-launch member participants

The initial cohort of active RTR system participants includes:

*   Wealthsimple
*   Questbank
*   Peoples Trust Company
*   Paramount Commerce
*   KOHO
*   DoBusiness.com™
*   Digital Commerce Bank
*   Bank of America

Canada’s deliberately sequenced [RTR rollout](https://www.payments.ca/systems-services/payment-systems/real-time-rail-payment-system/testing-and-launch) pairs day-one security with rapid scalability. With additional participants onboarding continually in the coming months, including all major Canadian financial institutions and other members applying for access, the RTR will be available to more than nine in 10 Canadians within the first year after launch.

### Made-in Canada, for Canada

The launch of the RTR reflects our ‘Team Canada’ approach, [bringing together regulators, members, stakeholders and delivery partners around a shared vision](https://www.payments.ca/new-source-strength-canadas-economy-canadas-real-time-rail-now-live). Built in Canada and designed to serve all Canadians, the RTR provides accessible payment infrastructure through existing banking and payment channels. This infrastructure supports a diverse country and a broad range of communities, including small businesses, newcomers and people in rural areas.

[Payments Canada research](https://www.payments.ca/insights/news-research?field_article_type=219) found that 60 per cent of Canadian businesses are ready to adopt real-time payments to address everyday challenges such as forecasting cash flow and waiting to send and receive funds. More than half of surveyed consumers (52 per cent) also expressed interest and intent to use real-time payments.

To meet this evolving need, the RTR serves as a secure platform for innovation. With it, system participants can build and offer products and services that benefit consumers and businesses across the country, supporting a changing economy and Canada's future prosperity.

### An infrastructure for the future

Canada’s Real-Time Rail is an important step toward a more productive, innovative and inclusive economy, and the work will continue to ensure the country’s payment infrastructure meets Canadians’ evolving needs.

Title: DeepX Tapes Out Second-Gen Chip, Projects 6.7× Performance Gain With LPDDR5x-PIM

URL Source: https://www.eetimes.com/deepx-tapes-out-second-gen-chip-projects-6-7x-performance-gain-with-lpddr5x-pim/

Published Time: 2026-11-09T06:47:26+00:00

Markdown Content:
South Korean edge AI chip startup DeepX has taped out its second-generation AI accelerator with access to custom processor-in-memory (PIM) technology from Samsung. The DX-M2 is designed to bring generative AI to robots, drones, and other edge devices, enabling inference of models with up to 100 billion parameters at less than 5 W.

DeepX’s first-generation chip, the DX-M1, is now in mass production, targeting vision applications. The newly taped-out DX-M2 aims to make local AI a practical choice for devices with tight power and thermal budgets. The chip is designed to run models with 20 billion to 100 billion parameters (approximately 3 billion to 20 billion active parameters) at 10 to 30 tokens per second, depending on the model. This is achieved within the same power budget as the M1—just 5 W.

“The most important change [between M1 and M2] is the memory bandwidth,” DeepX founder and CEO Lokwon Kim told EE Times.

Memory bandwidth has tripled from 50 to 150 GB/s, but there are several other efficiencies. DeepX said its NPU has doubled its power efficiency thanks to design improvements, and moving to a 2-nm process node doubled it again. 80 TOPS can now be achieved.

“This is important because with 5 W power consumption we can go everywhere, drones or any other battery-powered device,” Kim said. “Our goal is to enable deployment of sophisticated AI in all devices.”

The M2 can handle large mixture-of-experts LLMs and supports new techniques, including speculative decoding and TurboQuant.

DeepX’s Tim Park (left) and Lokwon Kim (Source: [DeepX](https://deepx.ai/))

### **Processor-in-memory**

Most types of AI inference operations are constrained by moving weights between memory and compute, especially GEMV (general matrix-vector multiplication), during which random memory accesses are required, slowing down computation. Memory makers have come up with PIM schemes in which memory-bound operations such as GEMV can be computed inside the memory chip. Doing operations within memory increases the effective memory bandwidth and reduces time-consuming memory access times.

PIM is set to become a JEDEC standard for LPDDR6. However, DeepX has been working with Samsung on integrating the DX-M2 with Samsung’s LPDDR5x-PIM.

“We have spent one and a half years on this technology, collaborating with Samsung Memory, as they already have their custom PIM for LPDDR5x,” Kim said. “We already received LPDDR5x PIM samples and we are testing the operations and performance in-house.”

DeepX’s simulations show that offloading GEMV operations from the DX-M2 into LPDDR5x-PIM will result in 6.7× the tokens per second for Llama3.1-8B versus the DX-M2 alone.

“DX-M2 with LPDDR5x-PIM is close to optimal,” Kim said. “But our next generation, the DX-M3, will support official LPDDR6 PIM technology; then we can get the full theoretical performance advancement, which is 5× to 8× higher performance.”

The only drawback, Kim explained, is that the extra compute doesn’t come for free—6.7× the performance needs 2.7× the power consumption overall. That said, DeepX thinks it can get a 2× performance uplift within the same power envelope as non-PIM operation.

“Substantial manual effort” is required in the compiler to support this mode of operation, Kim said, noting DeepX currently has a prototype compiler running, based on a simulation of the PIM-enabled LPDDR5x. “We are now making the hardware modules so that we can test that in the physical environment, so we couldn’t finish the compiler yet, but we are actively working on it.”

Offloading GEMV operations into memory will improve tokens per second by 6.7× (based on Llama3.1-8B), according to DeepX, at the expense of power consumption. (Source: DeepX)

### **Key markets**

The DX-M2 will target several key sectors. DeepX is working with Taiwanese OEMs to find the right sweet spot for AI PCs, including laptops and workstations. Robotics companies, currently prototyping on GPUs such as Nvidia Thor, want lower power and more compute on-device, and automotive companies are looking for a low-power chip that can run agents in-vehicle, Tim Park, director of strategic marketing at DeepX, told EE Times. For IoT devices, DeepX is already working with Samsung on a next-generation smart hub. The company is also joining the AWS IoT ecosystem so it can use Greengrass to support remote model updates.

Robotics customers typically begin development on GPUs but have to look for alternatives due to thermal and power consumption considerations, Park said. DeepX is working hard to enable transitions from the Nvidia Isaac robotics platform to its in-house equivalent, Newton.

“Robotics customers ask us about our hardware, but also about how they can migrate from Nvidia to DeepX,” he said. “This is the answer—customers change their APIs to call Newton instead of Isaac and then they can run the exact same pipeline on the DeepX system.”

DeepX has 17 compatible libraries up and running, Park said. The company has demonstrated M1-based robots using the same source code as an Nvidia Jetson-based robot, but calling the DeepX libraries.

“The actual outcome for the customer is they can enjoy 20 times longer battery life and [lower cost] when they switch from Nvidia to DeepX,” Kim said. “At the same time, the switching time can be under a second. They just need to change the API name from Isaac to Newton. That’s it.”

A full robotics stack for DeepX hardware is currently under development.

DeepX is engaging with robotics customers in the U.S., China, Vietnam, and Korea, while Hyundai Motor Group Robotics Lab is already using the DX-M1 in its robotics platform.

Meanwhile, the company is building out its ecosystem, adding Taiwanese OEMs, vertical champions in various markets and, lately, a collaboration with Intel.

DeepX is working with Intel to integrate OpenVINO with the DeepX SDK in order to tap into Intel’s x86 customer base. The DX-M1 can complement integrated NPUs in Intel Core Ultra CPUs and enable AI for other Intel edge CPUs that don’t have an NPU, offloading some or all of the AI workload.

The company recently met with AMD to discuss jointly developing a robotics platform based on DeepX accelerators combined with AMD’s Kria reference board, in particular for the Korean ecosystem, Kim said. This is part of DeepX’s drive to collaborate with other heterogeneous ecosystems, including Raspberry Pi and Baidu’s PaddlePaddle ecosystem.

DeepX has developed software libraries for robotics under the name DX-Newton. (Source: DeepX)

### **Commercial traction**

DeepX has more than 100 purchase orders for the DX-M1 so far, from all major global markets across all physical AI industries (including drones, robots, smart factory, surveillance camera, aerospace and defense, healthcare, and IoT), Kim said. The M1 is now in mass production.

The most active market for physical AI was previously China, Kim said, but Japan has emerged this year as a major market, with a strong willingness to pioneer humanoid robots.

“All the large Japanese companies are evaluating our chips, more than 10 leading companies in Japan right now, and their feedback is very encouraging,” he said. “At the same time, the U.S. market [is strong]; we have several big names there, and their feedback is really good.”

DeepX is also engaged in smart city projects in South Korea, Vietnam, and Singapore.

An artist’s rendering of the final DX-M2 chip, which has just taped out. (Source: DeepX)

“Our long-term view is that AI compute will become more distributed as efficiency improves,” Park said. “The PC and smartphone eras showed how computing can spread into many products. AI will follow its own path, but local inference has clear value when an application needs immediate access to sensor data or operation without continuous connectivity.”

DeepX considers edge AI to be a substantial opportunity for its chips, Park said, especially at a time when the amount of power available for new data centers is limited.

Kim’s belief is that just as only a quarter of the CPU market is in the data center today, the AI processor market will also shift to the edge in the next five to 10 years.

At a time when many AI data center projects are delayed, the AI capacity issue can’t be solved with investment alone, he added. AI chips that consume just 5 W can enable migration of AI to the device.

“If we deploy models up to 100 billion parameters in devices, we can reduce AI data center traffic by more than 80%,” Kim said. “That means we could have five times larger infrastructure without adding any AI servers. This is our vision.”

DeepX’s third-generation will be chiplet-based. (Source: DeepX)

On the roadmap for DeepX’s third generation is the DX-M3, coming in 2028. The M3 will be chiplet-based and will target 1 ePOPS (INT8) using LPDDR6-PIM. The main target markets for this are automotive OEMs and humanoid robotics companies, whose demands will require multi-chiplet designs.

In the meantime, samples of the M2 are expected in March 2027, with mass production targeted for fall 2027.

# The AI ‘credit card’ is getting costlier as CoreWeave bond yield tops 16%

Published Fri, Nov 6 2026 12:02 PM EST Updated Fri, Nov 6 2026 12:09 PM EST

Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email

Key Points

*   CoreWeave’s bond yield has climbed above 16%, highlighting investor concern about financing the AI infrastructure boom.
*   Default protection costs have risen across AI-linked companies, including Nvidia, Broadcom and Oracle.
*   Wall Street expects substantial borrowing to fund further AI expansion, making financing costs a key test for the spending boom.

In this article

Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT

Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty Images

Debt markets are sending a message to AI data center builders: we’re hiking the interest rate on your credit card and may put some new curbs on your credit limit.

That analogy comes courtesy of Jefferies global head of equity strategy, Christopher Wood, who put it in a note on Friday: “The most plausible way the AI capex arms race will end is that the credit card will be taken away.”

That isn’t happening yet, but credit markets have been spooked by the new political landscape — seeing more hurdles to data centers under Democratic governors in key states, along with a Democratic-controlled Congress.

The poster child for debt stress is neocloud [Coreweave](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CRWV/). The yield on its 2032 bond with a 9.625% coupon has climbed above 16%. Coreweave’s five-year credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points on Thursday, widening above their October peak, according to Deutsche Bank. The CDS eased 8% Friday to around 1,155.

“We’ve had plenty of warnings from the credit space,” said Jim Reid, Deutsche Bank’s global head of macro and thematic research, in a note on Friday. Debt and equities are now moving more in sync, he added, “so we’ll have to see if credit goes any further.”

Investors are demanding more compensation to insure against default among even companies with the strongest balance sheets and credit ratings, including [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/), [Broadcom](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AVGO/), and [Amazon.com](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMZN/).

CDS on Nvidia debt is up 76% in the last month. Broadcom’s CDS is up 49%, while Amazon’s has gained 44%. Their CDS remain low on an absolute basis; Nvidia’s spread stood at roughly 139 basis points, compared with about 298 bps for [Oracle](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ORCL/) and roughly 1,100 for CoreWeave. A large increase from a low starting point does not imply the same credit risk.

Still, rising CDS are a sign that markets want more protection against default among even the largest and healthiest debt issuers. And rising CDS imply higher financing costs down the line.

The market is now grappling with the prospect that at least some data center spending will be delayed or scrapped under incoming Democratic governors in Ohio, Texas, and Georgia, the three states with much of the planned capacity.

Moratoriums could impact 45% of planned capacity in the U.S. with a large amount of that in Texas, according to Goldman Sachs. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she’s not opposed to data centers but wants a moratorium until the state legislature passes protections for communities.

None of these means AI debt financing is collapsing. Goldman tallies five AI bond deals totaling $67 billion since October 29, pushing total hyperscaler debt issuance this year to $296 billion. Goldman forecasts $440 billion of hyperscaler debt issuance next year, plus an additional $300 billion of project-level issuance across investment-grade and high-yield.

The Trump administration is vowing to support data centers. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett [told CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/data-centers-ai-elections-hassett.html) on Friday that he expects data center growth to continue as forecast, despite Democrats’ big election wins.

**What comes next**

The big question now is how quickly AI spending will generate enough cash for hyperscalers to keep investors comfortable with future capex plans. For the neoclouds, any sign of consolidation or retrenchment in capex could result in fewer or shorter contracts for data center compute or delays in prepayments.

Goldman analysts said hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in the third quarter as capital spending exceeded operating cash flow.

“Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments—which we view as additional and sizable uses of cash, separate from Capex—are the key risks to more debt issuance, subject to market conditions,” according to the bank.

Peak AI debt issuance may now be closer at hand. Bank of America analysts estimates that AI-related credit issuance will rise 31% from 2026 to 2027, hitting $685 billion, including public and private debt. They then see it falling 23% to $531 billion in 2028.

As for the risk? “Downside to these forecasts exists from a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure projects on the back of the Blue Wave, which will reduce capex needs and thus debt market funding,” BofA said in a note.

Stevie Bonifield
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.
During Paramount Skydance’s
latest earnings call
, CEO David Ellison said “it’s hard to imagine” AI won’t have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company’s outlook for AI, Ellison said:
“I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history. The last time we saw anything close to this was really the, you know, advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 90s. That technology gave birth to amazing stories like
Jurassic Park
and
Terminator 2
, and it’s hard to imagine that AI is not going to have a more significant impact than that. And I personally believe that’s going to be an incredible unlock on creativity.”
Ellison gave
Terminator
as an example, describing how it cost $4 million to make, but “if you wanted to make that picture today, shot for shot, it’s $60 to 70 million.” He went on to suggest AI might be able to help with that: “We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budgets more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk.”
Related
James Gunn is out as DC movie leader
Paramount Skydance says it will offer HBO Max and Paramount Plus as a bundle starting in “early 2027.”
Skydance’s games division is laying off staff.
Ellison said AI will “significantly” reshape Paramount Skydance’s business, saying the company has been developing its own AI tools. As a result of those tools, Ellison claims, “content will be easier to produce, projects across the organization will speed up, and how we work will transform.” He emphasized that “all of this makes the value of premium IP and live events more valuable, not less.”
Ellison also noted that “in a world of AI slop, we think there will always be a premium for truly hand-crafted storytelling.” He added, “We also continue to believe that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists and will never be a replacement for them.”

Jay Peters
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
President Trump held a White House press briefing earlier today and responded to several questions about his knowledge of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang said
this weekend
that he had been “​​unfaithful” to his wife, and the company
has opened an investigation into Huang
.
Recent articles from
The New York Times
indicated that Trump had been aware of a relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, the suspected spy, before information about it became public. In October,
The New York Times
reported that
Trump had been briefed “roughly a year ago” on intelligence that Huang and the alleged spy, Alice Huang, had developed a close relationship, but he didn’t do anything with the information. Yesterday,
the
NYT
reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio helped draft a memo to Trump officials about the relationship before Trump visited China in May.
In the press conference, Trump wasn’t specific about when he learned of the affair. But Trump said Huang told him today that he had “no idea” the person was a spy.
Here are Trump’s responses to questions about Jensen Huang from his press briefing today. You can watch a replay of the press conference
on MS Now’s YouTube channel
.
When were you first informed that there was an issue with Jensen Huang and the affair? What was presented to you at the time?
I would say that when I heard about it, first of all, I was amazed because I view him as a very high-quality person. I’ve known him a long time. It’s the largest, by value, the largest or one of the largest companies in the world. He did that with a chip. When you think about it, you’ve got a chip that’s 10 years advanced, can’t be… the Blackwell can’t even be copied. He’s an amazing guy.
I just hope there’s no problem. If there is a problem, we’ll let you know about it. But I hope there’s no problem. I believe he’s suffering greatly. I read his statement. And I believe he’s suffering greatly. Moreso because of his family. His wife who he loves and his family. But he is definitely suffering.
Just to follow up on the, “When were you first told of these potential issues with Mr. Huang?” You didn’t answer that question.
Well I’ve been hearing about it, and I’ve been reading a little bit about it over a period of time. But, not too long ago.
When is that?
We’ll look into it. I know the FBI’s looking into it in terms of something else. I think that he’ll be in good shape.
…
Are you going to bring up the case of Jensen Huang with President Xi when you visit with him next week?
No, I don’t think so. Maybe, I’m sure, President Xi will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he’s a very honorable man. He built a great company. American company. I think he’s a very honorable guy. I feel very confident that he’ll be in good shape.
Sticking with Jensen Huang, when you went to China earlier this year in May, did you know about these alleged ties to the spy then?
No, I didn’t hear about it then. But a lot of people have heard about it. And Jensen totally denies that. I asked him today, because I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling alright, how are you doing… and I asked him about that. He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question, did you have any idea that she was a spy? He said, I had no idea that she was a spy. And I really believe him.
…
I want to put a finer point on when exactly you were made aware of the intelligence around Jensen Huang.
Oh, I’d have to check. But this has been going on…
But there are reports that Secretary Rubio put an intelligence memo out last year. Did you read that memo?
I’d certainly check with the intelligence people. It could have been mentioned. Certainly it didn’t make much of an impact on me.

Title: Claude Fable 5.2 launch offers

URL Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17506494-claude-fable-5-2-launch-offers

Markdown Content:
To mark the launch of Claude Fable 5.2, we’re giving subscribers on eligible paid plans extra Fable usage for a limited time. Plans and seats that include Fable models get one to three Fable resets based on how long they’ve subscribed. Plans and seats that use Fable models with usage credits get Fable models included for one week, plus one Fable reset. This article explains what each plan gets, how a Fable reset works, and how to use one.

## What each plan gets

Both offers start when Fable 5.2 launches on November 9, 2026. They cover every Fable model, including Fable 5.2, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5.

Resets go only to accounts with paid billing in place before November 9, 2026 at 10:00 am PT. For Team and Enterprise seats, the organization's billing must have been in place by then. Seat holders must also have joined the organization before then. If your subscription started before then but is still in a free trial, you get your resets once it converts to paid. Self-serve Team trials count as paid.

Resets have no cash value, can't be transferred, and may be removed for fraud, abuse, or violation of our terms.

## How a Fable limit reset works

A Fable limit reset does two things:

For example, say you’ve used 80% of your weekly limit: 50% on Fable models and 30% on other models. After a Fable reset, you’re back to 30% of your weekly limit. If your account has a five-hour limit, it’s fully refilled.

A reset doesn’t raise your limits. It restores usage so you can keep working within your existing limits.

Once you use a reset, you can't undo it. If you cancel or downgrade before using a reset, it's no longer available. For more information, see **[What is a limit reset?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17007452)**

## Fable limit resets based on subscription length

If you’re on a Max or Ultra plan, a premium seat on a Team plan, or a premium seat on a legacy seat-based Enterprise plan, the number of Fable resets you get depends on how long you’ve been a paid subscriber:

Subscription length is measured from the date of your first paid bill. If you subscribed through an app store, it’s measured from your first app store bill. If you canceled and came back, the time since your first paid bill still counts. On Team and Enterprise plans, subscription length is measured from your organization's first paid bill, so every premium seat in an organization gets the same number of resets.

These resets expire on March 8, 2027 at 11:59 pm PT. Any resets you haven’t used by then lapse. You can see the expiry date next to your resets in **[Settings > Usage](https://claude.ai/settings/usage)**.

## A week of Fable models included in your plan

If you’re on a Pro plan or a standard seat on a Team plan, all Fable models are included in your plan’s weekly usage limits from launch on November 9, 2026 through November 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm PT. During that week, you can use up to 50% of your weekly usage limits on Fable models at no extra cost, the same way plans that include Fable models can. After you use that 50%, or once the week ends, Fable usage is billed to usage credits if you have them turned on.

You also get one Fable limit reset if you meet the billing cutoff above. The reset expires on November 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm PT.

When the week ends, Fable models go back to running on usage credits on Pro plans and standard seats on Team plans. Learn more about **[Claude Fable models on your plan](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964)**.

## How to use a Fable reset

Your Fable usage is restored right away. You can use a reset at any time before it expires, not only when you’ve reached a limit.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a Fable limit reset raise my usage limits?

No, your usage limits stay the same, including the cap of 50% of your weekly usage limits on Fable models. A reset gives you back usage you’ve already spent, so you can use Claude more than you otherwise could before your limits reset next. It restores the Fable usage on your weekly limit and, if your account has a five-hour limit, refills that too.

### Which models does a reset cover?

Every Fable model: Fable 5.2, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5. The same goes for the one week of Fable access on Pro plans and standard seats on Team plans.

### What happens after the week of included Fable models?

Fable models go back to running on usage credits, and they no longer draw from your plan’s weekly usage limits. Any unused portion of the 50% allowance doesn’t carry over, and an unused reset expires at the end of the window.

### Why did I get fewer Fable limit resets than someone else?

The number of resets is based on how long you've been a paying Claude subscriber, measured at launch from your first paid bill (or your organization's on Team and Enterprise plans), even if you paused or switched plans since. Under six months gets one reset, six to 12 months two, and more than 12 months three.

### I canceled and resubscribed. How is my subscription length counted?

From your first paid bill, not from when you came back. A gap in your subscription doesn’t reset the clock.

### Does this apply to Team and Enterprise plans?

Standard seats on Team plans get a week of included Fable models plus one reset. Premium seats on Team plans and premium seats on legacy seat-based Enterprise plans get one to three Fable resets based on subscription length. Standard seats on legacy seat-based Enterprise plans, self-serve Enterprise plans, and usage-based Enterprise plans aren’t included.

### Can I use a Fable limit reset on other models?

On your weekly limit, a Fable limit reset only restores usage spent on Fable models. If your account has a five-hour limit, the reset refills all of it, including usage spent on other models.

### Can I use a Fable limit reset on my HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan?

No, Fable limit resets are not available for HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans.
